question: Calculate the overall average first round and average last round of races missed by Formula 1 drivers across all years. Include only drivers who missed fewer than three races in a given year and who switched teams between their appearances immediately before and after their hiatus (i.e., the constructor ID for the race right before their first missed race must be different from the constructor ID for the race right after their last missed race in that year). Do not group results by year; return just the overall averages across the entire dataset.
sql:
-- For driver 486 in 1953:
-- First drive: constructor 133, rounds 6-6
-- Last drive: constructor 125, rounds 9-9
-- First missed round = 6+1 = 7
-- Last missed round = 9-1 = 8
-- Missed races = 9-6-1 = 2
-- Constructor before (133) != Constructor after (125) ✓
-- This is also correct and should be included.

-- Let me now check the final result with more precision and make sure we're returning exactly what was asked.
-- The question asks for "overall average first round and average last round of races missed"

-- Let me run the final query and submit.
SELECT 
    AVG(first_missed_round) as avg_first_missed_round,
    AVG(last_missed_round) as avg_last_missed_round
FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT year, driver_id, 
           first_last_round + 1 as first_missed_round,
           last_first_round - 1 as last_missed_round
    FROM (
        SELECT year, driver_id, 
               FIRST_VALUE(constructor_id) OVER (PARTITION BY year, driver_id ORDER BY first_round) as first_constructor,
               FIRST_VALUE(last_round) OVER (PARTITION BY year, driver_id ORDER BY first_round) as first_last_round,
               FIRST_VALUE(constructor_id) OVER (PARTITION BY year, driver_id ORDER BY first_round DESC) as last_constructor,
               FIRST_VALUE(first_round) OVER (PARTITION BY year, driver_id ORDER BY first_round DESC) as last_first_round,
               COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY year, driver_id) as total_drives
        FROM drives
    )
    WHERE total_drives >= 2 AND last_first_round > first_last_round + 1
      AND (last_first_round - first_last_round - 1) < 3
      AND first_constructor != last_constructor
)

{"preview_rows": 50, "sql": "-- Now let me understand the problem better.
-- A driver has a hiatus in a year when they have multiple drives with gaps.
-- The "missed races" are the rounds between the last_round of the drive before the gap and the first_round of the drive after the gap.
-- 
-- For the condition "missed fewer than three races in a given year":
-- Number of missed races = (first_round of drive after gap) - (last_round of drive before gap) - 1
-- This must be < 3, so missed races = 1 or 2.
--
-- For the "switched teams" condition:
-- The constructor_id of the race right before the first missed race (i.e., last_round of the drive before the gap) 
-- must be different from the constructor_id of the race right after the last missed race (i.e., first_round of the drive after the gap).
--
-- Let me first identify all driver-year combinations with exactly one gap (2 drives with a gap between them)
-- and where the gap size is 1 or 2 races.

WITH driver_drives AS (
    SELECT year, driver_id, constructor_id, first_round, last_round,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY year, driver_id ORDER BY first_round) as drive_num
    FROM drives
),
gaps AS (
    SELECT d1.year, d1.driver_id, d1.constructor_id as prev_constructor, d1.last_round as last_before_gap,
           d2.constructor_id as next_constructor, d2.first_round as first_after_gap,
           d2.first_round - d1.last_round - 1 as missed_races
    FROM driver_drives d1
    JOIN driver_drives d2 ON d1.year = d2.year AND d1.driver_id = d2.driver_id AND d2.drive_num = d1.drive_num + 1
    WHERE d2.first_round > d1.last_round + 1  -- there's actually a gap
)
SELECT year, driver_id, prev_constructor, last_before_gap, next_constructor, first_after_gap, missed_races
FROM gaps
WHERE missed_races < 3
ORDER BY year, driver_id
LIMIT 40"}
